by: session, 20 Oct 2026, Surds clip 1 to the house rules

beats.say: Rationalize the denominator of two over root five plus root three.
Rationalizing means removing the surd from the bottom of the fraction. Here the bottom has two terms.
asks: Why remove the surd from the bottom?

beats.say: So the plan: the same value, written with no surd in the bottom.
When there are two terms below, multiply the top and the bottom by the conjugate.
asks: Why the top and the bottom?

beats.say: The conjugate is the same pair, with only the middle sign flipped.
asks: Which sign is the middle sign?

do.text: Conjugate: change only the middle sign

beats.say: Why it works: A plus B, times A minus B, always gives A squared minus B squared.
asks: Where does this rule come from?

beats.say: Squaring a surd removes its root. So after multiplying, the bottom has no surd left.
asks: Why does squaring remove the root?
Where do the middle terms go?

aside.text: Why does the conjugate clear the surd?
read: The two middle terms, $-\sqrt{15}$ and $+\sqrt{15}$, cancel.
**Plus times minus leaves only the two squares — no surd.**

beats.say: Write the fraction again, then times root five minus root three, over root five minus root three.
asks: Why put the conjugate on the top too?

beats.say: Plus becomes minus, and only the middle sign changes. Root five stays root five.
We multiply the top and the bottom by the same thing, so the value does not change.
asks: Why does the value stay the same?
Can I multiply only the bottom?

aside.text: Why does the value stay the same?
read: $\dfrac{\sqrt5-\sqrt3}{\sqrt5-\sqrt3}$ has the same top and bottom.
Multiplying only the bottom would change the value.

beats.say: Multiply the top with the top: two times root five minus root three.
And the bottom with the bottom: root five plus root three, times root five minus root three.
The bottom is A plus B, times A minus B. That always equals A squared minus B squared.
asks: Where does this rule come from?
What are A and B here?

beats.say: Here A is root five, and B is root three.
Expand the top: two root five minus two root three. The bottom: root five squared, minus root three squared.
asks: How do I expand the top?
Where did the middle terms go?

beats.say: A surd times itself is the number inside. So root five squared is five, and root three squared is three.
asks: Why is root five squared five?

beats.say: Five minus three is two. The bottom is now a number with no surd.
Split the fraction: each term over two.
asks: Can I leave it as one fraction?

beats.say: Divide each term by two: two root five over two is root five. So the answer is root five minus root three.
asks: Is there still a surd in the bottom?
Can I check with a calculator?
